visual_system: Clean, youthful telehealth look aimed at a younger demographic.
Conversion-led homepage: sign-up and patient portal are the main calls to action.
Light editorial footprint; most polish sits in the app, not in content.
site_architecture: Three-property setup: marketing site (easykind.com.au) plus app and portal subdomains.
Only a handful of marketing pages: home, pricing, contact, careers, a couple of guides.
Almost no programmatic surface; near zero location or condition pages.
tone_compliance: Sits a little in the grey; consultation framing is light in places.
Pricing is public and upfront, which suits a price-aware younger audience.
Thin disclaimers compared with the safer clinics.

steal.note: Brand demand funnels straight into app and portal.
Their portal sits very close to the brand search; we should mirror the funnel without copying the grey framing.

avoid.evidence: 9 ranking pages and 182 keywords, nearly all brand.
Pricing and product framing run ahead of disclaimers in places. Borrow the clarity, never the grey edges.
98% of traffic comes from brand spellings. A single non-brand displacement weakens the whole strategy.

implications: Easykind wins on brand demand, not search content; the non-brand gap is wide open.
Their volume comes from awareness, so location and condition pages are ours to take.
Match their pricing clarity, then out-publish them on education.

tagline: A brand-led, app-first clinic targeting a younger price-aware audience. Big on awareness, almost invisible in organic content.

eeat.notes: App polish does not extend to the content surface. No clinician bylines or medical-page schema. Pricing is public and clear — the strongest commercial signal on the site.
